messages:
jordan_support: heads up — acme-inc hit a bunch of decryption errors after last night's key rotation. customer sees InvalidCiphertextException and intermittent AccessDenied on KMS decrypts. high severity, they say production gen is failing. :frowning:

mike_security: :eyes: do we have cloudtrail events for their decrypt attempts? sounds like either encryption-context mismatch or grants not applied to the new key alias. any proxy in front of the client?

kira_crypto: can you paste the exact error strings and a minimal repro? also need aws cli outputs: `aws sts get-caller-identity`, `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key>` and a CloudTrail snippet if possible. encryption-context issues usually show up as AccessDenied with message referencing encryption context.

jordan_support: here's the error copy they sent:```InvalidCiphertextException: Ciphertext refers to a key that doesn't exist.\ncaused_by: aws.kms.DecryptFailed\n---\nAlso intermittently: AccessDeniedException: Caller is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345\nMessage: encryption context mismatch```They also included a short CLI repro they ran (redacted):```aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --region us-west-2```no --encryption-context specified.

sara_ops: quick check — our HSM/EME audit for that key shows decrypt RPCs from the customer's IAM role only before rotation time, but post-rotation I see very few decrypts and no successful decrypts logged for their principal. CloudTrail entry count drops to zero after rotation at 02:12 UTC.

mike_security: that suggests either their client stopped sending the encryption-context after rotation or the ciphertext now references a different KMS key id. Can we confirm the ciphertext metadata? if they re-encrypted under a new key or used alias swap, ciphertext will fail. Ask them for `openssl base64 -d -in ct.b64 | hexdump -C | head` or we can ask for the raw blob to inspect headers.

jordan_support: customer says they rolled the key via our rotation tooling which did an alias-point to new key id (k-02 -> k-03). They claim no re-encrypt on stored blobs. They rely on envelope encryption where the data key was rewrapped with new key on rotation — our job was supposed to rewrap but maybe the job failed.

kira_crypto: two paths: 1) If the ciphertext was rewrapped with new key, the decrypt must use the new key — that should be transparent to client unless encryption-context mismatched. 2) If the client-side SDK supplied an encryption-context at encrypt time and fails to supply the identical context at decrypt time, KMS will deny.

mike_security: ask customer to try a direct decrypt with explicit encryption-context echoed. Repro command:```aws kms decrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin \
  --encryption-context Usage=prod,App=acme-api \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345 \
  --region us-west-2```If that succeeds, it's an encctx mismatch. If it still fails with InvalidCiphertextException, the key id/ciphertext binding is wrong.

jordan_support: ran the explicit command for them with a sample context and got: `AccessDeniedException: encryption context mismatch` — so it's definitely encctx. The weird part: they claim they never set any encryption context at encrypt time.

sara_ops: could be their middleware / HTTP proxy stripping headers or our SDK version bug. I recall older AWS SDK for Java (1.x) had a bug where encryption context passed in headers could be lost when using certain proxies. What SDK and version are they on?

jordan_support: they say backend uses aws-java-sdk-core 1.12.47 through a sidecar that rewrites traffic via corp-proxy.

kira_crypto: that matches. Two action items: 1) Ask them to upgrade to latest SDK or set the encryption context explicitly via CLI to confirm. 2) On our side, check if the rotation job changed or added an encryption context in the rewrap operation (we do include a metadata tag sometimes). I also want CloudTrail event examples for their encrypt() calls before rotation — those show the original encryption-context if any.

mike_security: can we also run `aws kms list-grants --key-id <old-key>` and `--key-id <new-key>` to see if there are any grants tied to their cross-account role that didn't get migrated? missing grants could cause AccessDenied although the pattern here is encctx mismatch.

jordan_support: provided CloudTrail encrypt event pre-rotation:```{eventName: "Encrypt", userIdentity: {arn: "arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/acme-app/xyz"}, requestParameters: {encryptionContext: {Usage: "prod", App: "acme-api"}}}```so there was an encryption-context after all — they were unaware.

sara_ops: aha. so encrypt used encctx. decrypt must provide the exact same map. If the rewrap operation our rotation job performed added or changed encctx or if the client drop occurred, decrypt will fail. Also explains CloudTrail gap — the client's decrypt attempts may have been rejected early.

kira_crypto: suggested fix for customer: update client to pass the same encryption context on decrypt OR run a one-time rewrap that strips/preserves context consistently. If they want us to rewrap without encctx, we need a service ticket and explicit consent (audit & data retention).

mike_security: short-term mitigation: instruct customer to set their SDK to echo encryption context by adding the context map to decrypt calls. Example (Java):```Map<String,String> ctx = ImmutableMap.of("Usage","prod","App","acme-api");DecryptRequest req = new DecryptRequest().withCiphertextBlob(ByteBuffer.wrap(ct)).withEncryptionContext(ctx);```Long-term: add check in rotation job to preserve original encryption-context and emit an audit report of mismatches.

jordan_support: customer updated the service to include encctx on decrypt and reports success for some requests. Still seeing a small % failing for older archived blobs — those were encrypted years ago with an even older key and different context. Customer asked for list of affected objects so they can run a batch rewrap.

sara_ops: we can produce a list by scanning metadata store for key-id + encctx mismatch counts, but that requires a DB query. I'll open ops ticket and include sample SQL.

deploy-bot: rollback-notes: rotation-worker v2.14 rolled back to v2.12 at 03:10 UTC as a precaution. :white_check_mark:

mike_security: final notes — root cause: encryption-context was present during encrypts but not honored consistently during decrypts after rotation due to client SDK/proxy behavior and our rotation tooling not preserving metadata for certain archived blobs. Action items: 1) customer guided to add encctx to decrypt; 2) ops to run targeted rewrap for archived objects; 3) infra to add encctx-preserve/verify step to rotation pipeline; 4) produce audit report for affected keys.

jordan_support: closing loop with customer now. thanks all. :lock:
